findings.quote: A commissioner is a member like anyone else. They cannot move funds, cannot pay themselves, and cannot remove a member's ability to claim or to trigger a refund.
findings.reality: "Cannot pay themselves" is false in League mode. `post_payout_sheet` is commissioner-only (`has_one = commissioner`, programs/commish/src/lib.rs:1401-1403) and the only check on an assignee is that they are an existing paid Member of this pool (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:926-937). Nothing excludes the commissioner's own wallet, and the UI roster it is filled from is "every paid member" with no exclusion (src/components/LeaguePanel.tsx:95, 255). Once `finalize_sheet` runs (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:962-995) the commissioner calls `claim_prize` and the vault pays them (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:998-1066). A commissioner who joined their own league can assign themselves 100% of the sheet. The only obstacle is the member veto. The same is true in a weaker form in Survivor/Loser: the commissioner is the sole author of the winners mask (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:401-452), so they can post results that leave themselves the last member standing and then claim the pot. Separately, "a member like anyone else" is not right either: the commissioner holds three exclusive instructions (`post_results`, `post_payout_sheet`, `sponsor_join`).
findings.fix: Say that the commissioner cannot move funds to an arbitrary address, but that in a league they choose who is assigned each prize slot and may assign themselves, and that in a pick pool they author the results that decide who survives. State that the member veto is the only check on both.

findings.quote: We can pause the creation of new pools. We cannot pause a claim or a refund on a pool that already exists.
findings.reality: False as to a claim in a Survivor or Loser pool. `advance_week` names `fee_treasury_ata` as a required, typed `Account<'info, TokenAccount>` on every call, fee or no fee (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:1344-1349), so Anchor deserializes it before any of the program's own checks. `advance_week` is the only writer of `STATUS_SETTLED` for a pick pool (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:685), and `claim_pot` requires that status (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:747). The treasury is our address (scripts/init-config.ts:82). If that token account does not exist, no pick pool can ever settle and no winner can ever claim. The repo already knows this: the account list carries an "OPERATIONAL" warning that "a missing treasury ATA stops pools from settling" (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:1336-1343), and RunWeek pre-checks it with the message "The fee treasury has no USDC account, so the week cannot be closed" (src/components/RunWeek.tsx:157-165). An SPL token account with a zero balance can be closed by its owner, so this is a live lever, not a hypothetical. It does not let us take the money — `reclaim_dues` still works after the refund deadline (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:792-863) — but it does let us block a winner's claim indefinitely and force a pool to a pro rata refund instead. This also qualifies the absolute statements at lines 62 ("there is no moment at which we could stop it") and 117 ("we cannot freeze, reverse, seize, redirect or recover funds in a vault, for anyone, for any reason").
findings.fix: State the exception: every pick pool's settlement depends on our fee-treasury token account existing, and if it does not, no winner can claim until it does — the money then only comes out through the pro rata refund after the refund deadline. This is a live dependency on us, distinct from the upgrade-key disclosure already on the page, and worth a lawyer's eye given how much of the page rests on "we could not stop it".

findings.quote: Pools are private. They are joined by link. There is no public directory, no matchmaking, and no way for us or anyone else to browse for a pool to join.
findings.reality: The last clause is false. Every Pool account is enumerable with one `getProgramAccounts` call, and the site's own leaderboard does exactly that — it walks every Pool and every Member on the program (src/lib/leaderboard.ts:122-129). Nothing about joining requires a link or an invite: `check_join_open` tests only status, member count and deadline (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:1105-1123), and `JoinPool` takes no invite, allowlist or commissioner signature (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:1230-1250). The "link" is just /p/<pool address> with no secret in it (src/components/SharePool.tsx:29-35). The site's own Privacy Policy contradicts this sentence in terms: "That is not the same as a pool being private... Every pool record and every member record can be read straight off the blockchain by anyone, with one ordinary request to a public Solana node. No link needed. Our own leaderboard is built exactly that way." (src/app/privacy/page.tsx:54).
findings.fix: Keep "we publish no directory and no matchmaking" and drop "no way for us or anyone else to browse for a pool to join." Align with the wording already used on the Privacy Policy: joining is by link on this site, but pool and member records are public on chain and anyone who reads them can join an open pool.

findings.quote: sets the pool's rules, buy-in, schedule, prize structure, refund deadline and dispute window at creation, and cannot change several of them afterwards;
findings.reality: Two of the six are not the commissioner's to set. The refund deadline is computed by the site, not entered: for a pick pool it is week 18's lock plus 14 days (src/lib/schedule.ts:104-106, src/app/pools/new/page.tsx:266-270); for a league it is the dues deadline plus 30 days (src/app/pools/new/page.tsx:268-269). There is no refund-deadline field on the create form. The schedule is likewise fixed — `seasonLockSchedule` returns the committed real NFL schedule and ignores any anchor on a real clock (src/lib/schedule.ts:95-98, src/lib/season.ts:52-54); the commissioner picks only the start week. Also, "cannot change several of them afterwards" understates the program: there is no update-pool instruction at all, so none of them can be changed after creation.
findings.fix: List what the commissioner actually chooses (name, mode, buy-in, member cap, start week, dispute window, and in a league the dues deadline and prize split), say the lock schedule and refund deadline are fixed by the site, and say none of it can be changed after creation rather than "several".

findings.quote: After the pool's refund deadline has passed, any paid member can trigger a pro rata refund of the vault to the paid members.
findings.reality: `reclaim_dues` pays only the caller. It transfers to `member_ata`, which is constrained to be owned by the signing wallet (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:841-854, 1390-1395), and marks only that member claimed (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:856). The first caller fixes `refund_per_member` for everyone (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:833-836), but every other member still has to call it themselves. The UI says so plainly: "the vault pays each member directly" (src/components/ReclaimDues.tsx:151-155). Nobody's call refunds anyone else, and a member who never calls it is never paid.
findings.fix: Say each paid member reclaims their own share, that the first person to reclaim fixes the per-member figure for everyone, and that a member who never calls it is never refunded.

findings.quote: During that window, members can veto the posting.
findings.reality: `veto_results` has no time check at all. It requires only that the pool is in `STATUS_RESULTS_POSTED` or `STATUS_SHEET_POSTED` (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:463-467); nothing compares `now` against `pending_posted_ts + dispute_window_secs`. Because `finalize_week` and `finalize_sheet` are permissionless cranks that somebody has to actually call (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:540-555, 962-978), vetoes keep being accepted after the window has elapsed until someone cranks. The page understates the veto in one direction and misdescribes the deadline in the other: the real cut-off is whenever someone fires the finalize crank, not the window's expiry.
findings.fix: Say the window is the guaranteed minimum: a posting cannot be finalized before it closes, and votes are still accepted afterwards until somebody runs the finalize step.

findings.quote: If the window passes without a clearing majority, the results are finalized and the pool moves on.
findings.reality: Nothing happens on its own. `finalize_week` is a separate instruction that a person or script must call (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:540-581), and settling every member and closing the week are two more (`settle_member` at programs/commish/src/lib.rs:585-636, `advance_week` at programs/commish/src/lib.rs:639-734). The site exposes all three behind one "Run week" button that anyone can press (src/components/RunWeek.tsx:1-20, 145-215). If nobody presses it the pool sits in `STATUS_RESULTS_POSTED` indefinitely — which is exactly the abandonment case the deadman refund exists for.
findings.fix: Say that after the window closes, anyone can run the step that finalizes the week and moves the pool on, that it is not automatic, and that a pool nobody runs falls to the refund path after the refund deadline.

findings.quote: The window is chosen when the pool is created, must be between one hour and seven days, and is 48 hours if the pool does not choose.
findings.reality: The raw range check is 1 hour to 7 days (programs/commish/src/constants.rs:90-94), and 48 hours is the form's prefill (programs/commish/src/constants.rs:88, src/app/pools/new/page.tsx:82-84). But for a Survivor or Loser pool the program also requires every gap between weekly locks to exceed `MIN_POST_DELAY_SECS + dispute_window_secs` (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:201-215, programs/commish/src/rules.rs:80-84). The shortest gap in the committed 2026 schedule is 143.75 hours (weeks 11 to 12, src/data/nfl-schedule-2026.json), so anything at or above 140.75 hours — about 5.86 days — is rejected with BadDisputeWindow. Seven days is only reachable in a league pool, which has no lock schedule. The program's own test says as much: "At the 7-day maximum window nothing on a weekly schedule can pass" (programs/commish/src/rules.rs:196-198).
findings.fix: Say the program's range is one hour to seven days, but that a Survivor or Loser pool on the season schedule is limited to roughly five and a half days because each week has to leave room to post and finalize before the next lock.

findings.quote: read the leaderboard section of it particularly carefully before you opt in: that choice is public, global and permanent.
findings.reality: The listing itself is not permanent. The listing route accepts a signed "remove me" in the same shape as the opt-in and calls `setListed(wallet, false)` (src/app/api/auth/listing/route.ts:1-12, 66-82; src/lib/identity.ts:329). The Privacy Policy this sentence points to is precise about the distinction — "Being listed on the public leaderboard is global and permanent in effect" and "You can opt out of the leaderboard at any time. We will remove you from the page. We cannot remove the pairing from anyone who already recorded it" (src/app/privacy/page.tsx:122, 133). The Terms compress that into a flat "permanent," which describes the disclosure, not the setting.
findings.fix: Match the Privacy Policy's phrasing: the listing can be turned off at any time, but the handle-to-wallet pairing it publishes cannot be un-published.

missingDisclosures: A missed pick eliminates you. `rules::survives` returns false for any member with no pick for the finalized week, in both Survivor and Loser, with no grace (programs/commish/src/rules.rs:45-51, and the test at rules.rs:114-118). The page says only that "a wrong pick normally ends your run" and never mentions failing to pick at all.

A tie is a loss for both sides. The program has only a winners mask and a pushes mask; an unmarked team is a loss, and the results form deliberately records a tie as neither (src/components/ResultsForm.tsx:22-25, 122-140, 152-155, and the UI text "a tie is a loss for both" at ResultsForm.tsx:334). The page never mentions ties.

A cancelled or voided game is a push: it carries whoever picked either side in both modes, and still consumes that team for the season (programs/commish/src/rules.rs:37-56, programs/commish/src/lib.rs:613-615). The page never mentions pushes.

A team can only be used once per season in Survivor and Loser — `submit_pick` rejects a team already in `used_mask` (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:381), and teams on a bye are unpickable because an unmarked team reads as a loss (src/lib/season.ts:61-77). The page describes the pick as "one team you think will win" and says nothing about either constraint.

How a pick pool is decided when there is no single survivor. `advance_week` has three shapes (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:658-666): if everyone alive is eliminated in the same week, the pot is split among those who were alive at the START of that week; if more than one member survives week 18, they split it; only the one-survivor case is winner-take-all. The page says nothing about splits.

Once a pool reaches STATUS_SETTLED the deadman refund is closed forever — `reclaim_dues` requires `status != STATUS_SETTLED` (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:800) while `claim_pot` requires it (lib.rs:747). A winner who never claims leaves their share in the vault with no path out for anyone, by design rather than by bug. The page's lock-up warning is framed only as "a bug in this program could result in funds being locked."

`sponsor_join` lets the commissioner create a Member for an arbitrary wallet and pay that wallet's buy-in, with only the commissioner signing (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:317-359, 1252-1273). A wallet can therefore be enrolled in a pool it never signed for, and the record permanently shows who paid (`sponsored_by`). The page's account of joining assumes the member acts for themselves.

Creating a pool locks SOL rent that is never recoverable. The Pool account is 1,616 bytes (programs/commish/src/state.rs:244) plus an associated token account for the vault, both paid by the commissioner at creation (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:1204-1223), and there is no close-pool instruction anywhere — `close =` appears once in the whole program, on CloseMember (lib.rs:1428). The page says only that "network fees are payable to the Solana network," which does not cover a permanently locked rent deposit. Members can recover their own Member-account rent via `close_member` once the pool is settled or abandoned (lib.rs:1069-1082); commissioners cannot recover the pool's.

A commissioner can re-post a vetoed result or sheet without limit, and each re-post resets the vote — members must muster a fresh strict majority every time (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:436-441, 946-950; state.rs:108-119). The page says "a re-post is a new vote" but does not say the loop is unbounded, which is the practical cost to members of the only correction mechanism on offer.

The program pins one canonical USDC mint compiled into the binary and refuses any other at pool creation (programs/commish/src/constants.rs:14-17, lib.rs:131-135). Pools cannot be denominated in anything else, and a pool created against the wrong build cannot be joined at all.

Only three of the nine pool types in the program are enabled; the rest are refused at runtime with ModeNotEnabled (programs/commish/src/constants.rs:100-114, lib.rs:130). Pool size is capped at 2 to 500 members and 8 prize slots (constants.rs:24, 30-31), and a league's prize slots must sum to exactly 100% at creation (lib.rs:170-173).

`update_config` lets the admin pause creation of ALL new pools program-wide, not just on this site, and change the default fee and cap that future pools copy (programs/commish/src/lib.rs:83-99, 251-258). The page discloses the fee half and describes pausing as a site power ("We may... stop new pools being created"); it does not say the pause is an on-chain, program-wide switch we hold.
